per_shot.note: Real hab shell now: paneled ceiling with beams and strip fixtures, riveted wall panels, conduit, ribs, red trim, floor plating; fixture cones land on the wall, but it is one brown-sepia value family and the bottom 40% is empty dark floor.
Structure reads, dusk portholes are lovely, but stations hug the back wall in a wide murky room; light pools on the floor are faint and the porthole dusk does not reach the floor.
Same shell; corkboard adds life, the dark doorway at right is a heavy black block, and the room still feels dim rather than sanctuary-warm.
Clearly richer than stock: patterned rug, fern, radio with lit dial, books on a lit shelf all read as themselves; warm pools around them; suit is the brightest thing.
Best frame: arc lamp throws a genuine warm pool on wall and floor, star chart glows blue as an accent, books read; still a large empty dark floor plane below.

Galley kettle and cups, bunk with bedding and reading lamp, Gallery door glimpse all read well, but large blurry orange/pink smears on the floor (left and right foreground) look like reflection artifacts, not light.

top_issues.issue: Blurry orange/pink smears on the foreground floor
top_issues.why: They read as rendering artifacts (screen-space reflection or bloom ghosts of the arc lamp and Gallery light), not as light landing; they muddy the cleanest part of the frame.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Kill or heavily dampen floor reflections of off-axis lights; if a reflection is wanted, make it a tight, vertical streak directly under the source, matching the low-poly look.

top_issues.issue: The foreground floor is a huge, near-empty dark plane
top_issues.why: Roughly the bottom 35-40% of every frame is dim brown plating with little value change, so the room reads as a wide dark void with furniture lined against the back wall, not as a cosy lived-in hab.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Without changing the camera: warm the front floor with light falloff from the room (stronger pools reaching toward the viewer), add floor-level detail strips, a runner or inset panel line, cable trays or kick-lights along the front lip, and let the foreground fall to dark only at the very edge.

top_issues.issue: One sepia value family across wall, ceiling and floor
top_issues.why: Material structure is now present, but walls, ceiling and floor share the same brown-beige at similar values, so the stock DUSK room still feels somewhat monochrome and dim, more grim than sanctuary; the brief asks for value variation across surfaces.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Separate surfaces by value and temperature: lighter, warmer insulated wall panels where the cones hit; a darker, cooler floor; a mid-value ceiling with brighter fixture lenses; a few cooler accents (teal screen light, porthole sky) to make the warm read warmer.

top_issues.issue: Porthole dusk does not spill into the room
top_issues.why: The dusk discs are the best mood element (they echo the warm window of 02-surface) but they stay painted-on; the brief asks for dusk light from the portholes on the floor.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft, warm-orange elongated light patch on the floor and lower wall under each porthole, plus a faint glow ring on the porthole rim.

top_issues.issue: Furniture is small against a tall, wide room
top_issues.why: Bought items read but occupy a thin band along the back wall; the furnished room is richer but not yet dense or intimate enough to feel lived-in.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep slots, but give each furnishing its own small practical or contact pool, wall-hung companions (a pinned photo, hooks, a shelf bracket) and slightly larger presence so the band between floor and porthole line feels full.

protect: The real ceiling: paneled with beams and strip fixtures that cast cones onto the wall; never return to a black slab
